''' Raimonds Vējonis''' ({{IPA|lv|ˈrajmɔnts ˈvæːjuɔnis|}}; born 15 June 1966) is a Latvian politician who served as the 9th [[President of Latvia]] from 2015 to 2019 and the president of the [[Latvian Basketball Association]] since 2020.

He is a member of the [[Latvian Green Party]], part of the [[United List]]. He served as Minister of Environmental Protection and Regional Development in 2002 and in 2011 and as Minister of the Environment from 2003 to 2011, while the Ministry of Regional Development was a separate department. He became [[Minister of Defence of Latvia]] in 2014 and held that office until becoming president in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.mk.gov.lv/en/mk/sastavs/vejonis/ |title=The Cabinet of Ministers of the Republic of Latvia: Raimonds Vējonis |publisher=[[Cabinet of Ministers of the Republic of Latvia]] |access-date=2010-04-17 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101119024151/http://www.mk.gov.lv/en/mk/sastavs/vejonis |archive-date=2010-11-19 }}</ref> Since 2020 he is the president of  [[Latvian Basketball Association]].

==Early life and career==
[[File:Readout of Vice President Biden’s Meeting with President Raimonds Vējonis of Latvia (29164520746).jpg|thumb|Vējonis with U.S. Vice President [[Joe Biden]] in Washington, D.C., on 23 August 2016]]
Vējonis was born on 15 June 1966 in [[Pskov Oblast]] to a Latvian father and a Russian mother, while his father was serving in the [[Soviet army]] there. He grew up in [[Sarkaņi Parish|Sarkaņi]] and attended school in the nearby town of [[Madona]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.diena.lv/raksts/sestdiena/vejonis-militari-zalais-kompromiss-14045230/|title=Vējonis - militāri zaļais kompromiss|last=Zirnis|first=Egīls|date=21 February 2014|publisher=[[Diena]]|language=lv|access-date=3 June 2015}}</ref> Vējonis became interested in environmental protection because his grandfather had been blinded by chemicals used on a Soviet [[kolkhoz]].<ref name=afp>{{cite news|last1=Collier|first1=Mike|last2=Sibierski|first2=Mary|title=Latvia elects Vejonis, EU's first Green president|url=https://news.yahoo.com/latvian-parliament-elects-defence-minister-vejonis-president-153807530.html|access-date=5 June 2015|agency=Agence France-Presse|publisher=[[Yahoo!]]|date=3 June 2015}}</ref>

He graduated from Faculty of Biology of the [[University of Latvia]] in 1989 and obtained a master's degree from it in 1995. During his studies he worked as a biology teacher in Madona. From 1989 to 1996 he was deputy director of Madona Regional Environmental board. He was a member of Madona city council from 1990 to 1993. From 1996 to 2002 he was director of Greater Riga Regional Environmental board, during this period he also was a board member in [[Skulte, Skulte Parish|Skulte]] port and served as state representative at Getliņi Eko waste management company.<ref name="par">{{cite news|url=https://www.lsm.lv/lv/raksts/latvija/zinas/jaunais-latvijas-valsts-prezidents-raimonds-vejonis.a132288/|title=Jaunais Latvijas Valsts prezidents - Raimonds Vējonis|date=3 June 2015|website=Lsm.lv|language=lv|access-date=4 June 2015}}</ref>

==Political career==
In 2002, Vējonis became Minister of Environmental Protection and Regional Development.<ref name=englsm>{{Cite news|last=Collier|first=Mike|url=https://eng.lsm.lv/article/politics/president/latvia-provides-eus-first-green-president-raimonds-vejonis.a132316/|title=Latvia provides EU's first "green" president - Raimonds Vējonis|date=June 3, 2015|publisher=[[Public Broadcasting of Latvia]]|access-date=June 4, 2015}}</ref>

He was [[2015 Latvian presidential election|elected]] as [[President of Latvia]] on 3 June 2015, receiving the votes of 55 of the 100 members of the [[Saeima]].<ref name="par" /> He used his victory speech to promise to ensure national security, in light of [[War in Donbas (2014–2022)|events in Ukraine]], while protecting the environment.<ref name=afp /> He became the first head of state in the European Union to be a member of a [[green party]].<ref name=afp /><ref name=englsm />

== Post-presidency ==
In January 2020, Vējonis was elected to a four-year term as president of the [[Latvian Basketball Association]] by a wide margin.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://eng.lsm.lv/article/culture/sport/raimonds-vejonis-becomes-a-president-again.a345578/|title=Raimonds Vējonis becomes a president again|website=eng.lsm.lv|language=en|access-date=2020-04-28}}</ref> He was elected in the [[2026 Latvian parliamentary election|2026 elections]] to the [[Fifteenth Saeima of Latvia|15th Saeima]]. He became a Deputy Speaker of the Saeima.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.saeima.lv/lv/aktualitates/ievelets-15-saeimas-prezidijs/|title=Ievēlēts 15. Saeimas Prezidijs
|website=Saeima.lv|language=lv|access-date=2026-11-03}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
In 1986, he married [[Iveta Vējone]], a teacher and former first lady. The couple have two sons, Ivo and Nauris.<ref name=afp/> 
Vejonis speaks fluent Russian<ref>{{cite web|url=https://foreigncy.us/set/latvias-president-accent-raimonds-vejonis/|title=Latvia's "President with an Accent:" Raimonds Vejonis|website=Foreigncy.us|access-date=27 January 2019}}</ref> and decent English in addition to Latvian.

===Health problems===
On 18 January 2016, Vējonis was hospitalized. He was first transported to the Toxicology and [[Sepsis]] Clinic of the Riga East Clinical University Hospital branch Gaiļezers, but a day later was transferred to the Latvian Cardiology Center at [[Pauls Stradiņš Clinical University Hospital]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://skaties.lv/zinas/latvija/vejonis-sorit-nogadats-gailezera-slimnica/|title=Vējonis šorīt nogādāts Gaiļezera slimnīcā|website=Skaties.lv|access-date=27 January 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tvnet.lv/5106081/prezidenta-veselibas-stavokli-verte-ka-apmierinosu-nozimeta-arsta-uzraudziba|title=Prezidenta veselības stāvokli vērtē kā apmierinošu; nozīmēta ārsta uzraudzība|date=18 January 2016|website=Tvnet.lv|access-date=27 January 2019}}</ref> The press counselor of the president initially did not disclose the nature of the illness and suggested that the president had a viral infection. However, independent medical experts theorized that Vējonis probably had an [[infective endocarditis]]. On 20 January Vējonis underwent emergency [[Cardiac surgery|open heart surgery]] to eliminate the source of infection in which the heart valve damaged by [[sepsis]] was replaced with an [[artificial heart valve]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Paparde|first1=Inga|title=Kardioķirurgi glābj prezidentu|url=http://nra.lv/latvija/161012-kardiokirurgi-glabj-prezidentu.htm|access-date=2 February 2016|publisher=NRA|date=21 January 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lsm.lv/raksts/zinas/latvija/prezidenta-vejona-sirds-operacija-noslegusies.a165035/|title=Prezidenta Vējoņa sirds operācija noslēgusies|website=Lsm.lv|access-date=27 January 2019}}</ref> Later on unnamed sources told the press that the illness was likely caused by untreated [[tonsillitis]], the press counselor of the president, while still refusing to disclose exact diagnosis, confirmed that the president had been having issues with his throat and his voice had been very hoarse.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Cielava|first1=Ieva|title=Kas apdraudēja prezidenta sirdi? (preciz.)|url=http://www.irlv.lv/en/2016/1/26/kas-apdraudeja-prezidenta-sirdi|access-date=2 February 2016|website=Ir.lv|date=26 January 2016|archive-date=25 October 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171025022625/http://www.irlv.lv/en/2016/1/26/kas-apdraudeja-prezidenta-sirdi|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Vējonis left hospital on 26 February to undergo [[physical therapy]] at National Rehabilitation Center "Vaivari".<ref>{{cite news|url=https://eng.lsm.lv/article/politics/president/president-vejonis-to-leave-hospital.a170995/|title=President Vējonis to leave hospital|date=February 26, 2016|publisher=[[Public Broadcasting of Latvia]]|access-date=April 1, 2016}}</ref> He was reported to be doing some work during his illness, but fully resumed his official duties on 30 March after spending more than two months recovering.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://eng.lsm.lv/article/politics/president/president-to-resume-duties-next-week.a174923/|title=President to resume duties next week|date=March 23, 2016|publisher=[[Public Broadcasting of Latvia]]|access-date=April 1, 2016}}</ref>
